subject: Recap: Novapoint pilot scoping — SDK adapters, streaming fallback, structured outputs
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Clare Kim <clare@novapoint.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Novapoint pilot scoping — SDK adapters, streaming fallback, structured outputs

Hi Clare (and team),

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciate the clarity on the support-triage workflow and the two high-level goals: reduced time-to-first-response for agents, and better automated routing to the right resolver using reranking. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Key pain points you described:
- Slow semantic search: current vector store lookup + host-side reranker takes ~400-600ms per query, spikes during peak hours.
- Hard to reason about partial answers in streaming UI; you want progressive suggestions and a graceful fallback when streaming isn’t available.
- Tight throughput requirement for triage: ~250 qps at 90th percentile, with tail latency SLO of <200ms for embeddings lookup + rerank.

Goals we aligned on:
1) Pilot (4 weeks) validating: embedding + rerank flow, streaming-based progressive answers to agents, and an SDK shim that integrates with your VectorStore (we’ll support a small adapter).
2) Clear metrics: P95 latency for end-to-end inference, recall@10 for reranker, cost per 1M queries estimate.

Technical fit / considerations we discussed:
- SDK changes: small adapter (~100 LOC) to wire your vector store calls into Redwood’s embed + rerank endpoints. We’ll provide a test harness.
- Function calling: map your internal ticket-metadata (ticket_id, customer_id, priority) to structured func-call inputs; we recommend a narrow schema to start so the reranker can condition on ticket priority.
- Streaming: we’ll enable streaming with a chunked JSON-lines protocol. If a streaming connection drops, client should fall back to non-streaming endpoint — we’ll include a progress token so the UI can merge partial results.
- Structured outputs: propose a JSON schema for agent suggestions: {"suggestions": [{"id":"","score":0.0,"summary":"","actions":[...] }], "meta": {}} (we’ll iterate).
- Embedding & rerank model choices: start with our mid-size emb model for cost balance and a lightweight cross-encoder reranker for final scoring. We can recommend quantized variants if you prefer lower cost.

Attachments I said we’d send: example_payloads.json (sample request/response), quick SOW template, and a minimal SDK diff.

Action items (owners & timelines):
- Ben: produce SDK adapter diff + test harness by 2026-10-09. (Ben: include example vector-store mock and instructions to run locally.)
- Monica: draft commercial pilot SOW and pricing estimate by 2026-10-08.
- Jordan: provide recommended JSON schema for structured suggestions and an initial performance target matrix by 2026-10-07.
- Clare: share a representative export (anonymized) of 1k tickets + current ranking signals and confirm the vector store type.

If that aligns, we’ll lock the pilot scope and I’ll ask our infra team to reserve capacity for a 4-week pilot in us-west.

Thanks — next sync? If convenient, we can do a tech run-through next Tuesday (2026-10-12) at 11am PT.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: example_payloads.json (application/json), Novapoint_SOW_draft.pdf (pdf)

From: Clare Kim <clare@novapoint.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: sales@novapoint.ai
Date: 2026-10-05T16:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Novapoint pilot scoping — SDK adapters, streaming fallback, structured outputs

Jordan — thanks for the thorough recap. This matches our notes and I appreciate the clear owners. A few clarifications from my side: 

- Vector store: we run a managed FAISS cluster behind a microservice (proprietary wrapper). We can provide a mocked endpoint for the adapter.
- Important ranking signal: historical resolution_time (we’d like the reranker to bias toward shorter expected resolution when confidence is similar).
- Data sensitivity: the pilot data can be pseudonymized; we will not provide PII.

I’ve attached the SOW draft and a zipped sample payload set (anonymized). The SOW includes the target success criteria — notably, we need a measurable improvement in first-contact resolution within the pilot or we don’t proceed to an expanded commitment.

We’re good with the internal dates you proposed. Confirming: tech walkthrough on 2026-10-12 11am PT works.

On the attachments: could Ben include a small example of how the streaming fallback token would look in the SDK response? That will help our frontend engineers plan the UI merge.

Thanks,
Clare
Head of Product, Novapoint

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-05T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Novapoint pilot — immediate tasks

Ben/Monica — looping you in with Clare’s confirmations. Short internal asks: 

Ben:
- Please prototype the SDK adapter pattern (adapter interface + sample mock of our embed/rerank calls). Keep it a single-file diff if possible (we want it easy to review). Also include an example streaming fallback token shape (Clare asked for that).
- Run a small latency sanity run on a tiny mock set and capture p95/p99. Drop raw CSV to the Drive link in a folder named /novapoint/pilot/benchmarks.

Monica:
- Draft a 4-week SOW (trial) with optional expansion terms and pilot acceptance criteria tied to recall@10 and agent FCR improvement. Use conservative pricing for seat & usage.

I’ll draft the structured output schema and post to the Drive by EOD tomorrow.

Jordan

Quoted earlier: "Action items (owners & timelines)"

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Clare Kim <clare@novapoint.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Novapoint pilot scoping — SDK adapters, streaming fallback, structured outputs

Jordan / Monica / Clare — quick status: 

- SDK adapter: initial diff attached (sdk_patch.diff). It implements a VectorStoreAdapter interface and a local mock server you can run with `npm run mock-vs`. The adapter transforms the vector query + metadata into a Redwood embed call and formats the reranker input.
- Streaming fallback token: included in the example response as "stream_token": "s_tok_01|offset=128|partial=true" — frontend can use offset to request the remaining content via the non-streaming endpoint if needed. I also added a small example in example_payloads.json showing how the client merges partial suggestions.
- Benchmarks: small synthetic run attached (benchmarks.csv). Observed end-to-end P95 of 210ms on dev hardware (we’ll optimize kernels and batching).

ETA: I’ll push a cleaned PR and instructions by EOD 2026-10-09.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sdk_patch.diff (text), benchmarks.csv (text)
